messages:
Iris: Tiny governance question: do we have an official policy about the elevator button etiquette? There's a lot of passive-aggressive tapping at 17:59.
Marco: This is the hill I will die on. Single press only. If the doors close on you, that's a life lesson.
Danielle: Also can we stop holding the doors open for people who sprint across the lobby wearing backpacks? I feel personally attacked.
Omar: ElevatorBot: FYI average door-hold time last week was 11.2s. Please be courteous.
Sasha: Proposal: a friendly elevator pact. Rules: 1) single press, 2) no dramatic door-holding, 3) wave if you can't make it.
Iris: Love it. Addendum: If you press the close button and the doors stay open, you owe the next rider a coffee.
Marco: Counterproposal: if you press the close button and the doors close before the person reaches the door, you must perform a 3-second apology bow.
Danielle: Can we codify this with emoji reactions? :raising_hand: = I agree, :coffee: = I sponsor the coffee fund.
Omar: ElevatorBot: new feature suggestion accepted: auto-schedule "elevator etiquette" reminder at 4:50pm on Fridays.
Sasha: Historically the Close Button is decorative. I feel seen.
Iris: Also important: no conference calls in the elevator. You're creating a soap opera.
Marco: Noted. Also banning monologues about weekend vegan baking in the elevator. That's a personal dream-killer.
Danielle: For enforcement, I nominate a rotating role: Elevator Marshal. Duties: gentle reminders, ceremonial wave enforcement, and tallying door apologies.
Omar: PeopleOps: can we add Elevator Marshal as a micro-volunteer role? It's light-touch, 1 week rotation.
PeopleOps: Yes, we can. We'll add it to the micro-volunteer board and auto-assign if there are no volunteers.
Sasha: Suggestion: the Marshal gets a tiny badge (sticker) to wear for the week. We need badges for culture.
Iris: I will design a sticker. Theme: "Keeper of Doors" with a small cartoon elevator.
Marco: Enforcement mechanism idea: if you break a pact rule thrice, you must bring snacks for the next team stand-up. Harsh but fair.
Danielle: Snack-based justice is my favorite kind of justice.
Omar: ElevatorBot: tracking infra note 12; anonymous violation reports accepted via DM to bot.
Sasha: Also, what about pets? No pets in elevator during spike times. Tiny dogs are terrifying between floors.
Iris: Agreed. "No surprise pet floats" clause added.
Marco: Fun enforcement add-on: three violations earns you honorary placement on the "Hall of Shame" (temporary, light-hearted, expires after a week).
Danielle: Hall of Shame should be a digital sticker wall, not physical. No one needs more paper.
PeopleOps: We'll draft a micro-policy doc and circulate. This will include: etiquette, marshal rotation sign-up, snack consequences, and how to report infractions.
Omar: For rollout: pilot this week. Volunteer Marshals: I'll take Monday, Sasha Tuesday, Iris Wednesday.
Sasha: I'll create the sticker art and drop it in #design-requests. Low-key but iconic.
Iris: Also planning a tiny ceremonial bell for the Marshal to ring when the pact is upheld. Highly symbolic.
Marco: Will Marco be allowed to bow if close-button accidents happen? I will accept that fate.
Danielle: Reminder: be kind. Most people miss the elevator because of life stuff, not villainy. Pact is about courtesy, not policing.
Iris: Amen. Quick fun poll: which snack for the initial "pact enforcement" treat? :pretzel: pretzels, :cookie: cookies, or :banana: bananas?
Marco: :pretzel: for salty solidarity.
Danielle: :cookie: because sugar bonds teams.
Sasha: I'll bring pretzels and make tiny paper badges. Deal?
Omar: Pretzels it is. ElevatorBot: scheduling pretzel delivery for Friday 16:45 if guardrails pass.
PeopleOps: Thanks everyone. Draft micro-policy will be posted tomorrow. Thanks to the volunteers.
Iris: Motion passed by emoji consensus. Long live the Elevator Pact. May doors be fair and short. :door:
